source.title: Decoupling Semantic Similarity from Spatial Alignment for Neural Networks
source.authors: Tassilo Wald; Constantin Ulrich; Gregor Koehler; D. Zimmerer; Stefan Denner; M. Baumgartner; F. Isensee; P. Jaini; K. Maier-Hein

record.tranche_reason: The study's own experiments show that measured similarity changes with the construction of the representational similarity matrix, kernel, and dataset, refining how representation comparisons should be interpreted.
record.gate_note: The study compares spatially aligned and permutation-invariant representational similarity matrices (RSMs), using retrieval, correlations with classifier output similarity, and CKA analyses. It does not test convergence with model scale, cross-modal alignment, or recurring features. Values from cited work are not included. The paper also reports many approximation runtimes and matching-quality results, which do not measure the claim versions and are not rows.
record.test_reason: Only the appendix cross-model CKA comparison (Fig. 17) bears on a version. CKA between separately trained ResNets on CIFAR100 changes with RSM construction: spatio-semantic RSMs give higher cross-model similarity than semantic RSMs. That is a narrow, qualitative test of V6. The main experiments (retrieval, output-JSD correlation) measure within-model sample-to-sample similarity, not convergence between models.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that spatio-semantic RSMs couple semantics to spatial alignment, and that permutation-invariant semantic RSMs better capture semantic similarity (retrieval, output-similarity correlation). For CKA they show only qualitative changes, mostly modest, and lower cross-model similarity under semantic RSMs. They explicitly decline to recommend which RSM to use for inter-model CKA, citing a lack of benchmarks.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes permutation-invariant semantic RSMs, using set matching to construct sample similarities, rather than reproducing the original convergence studies' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with RSM construction (spatio-semantic versus permutation-invariant semantic), kernel (cosine, inner product, RBF), dataset (EgoObjects, Cityscapes, ImageNet, Tiny-ImageNet, CIFAR100), and—in retrieval—database size. The authors report that EgoObjects retrieval improvements decrease as database size grows.

fits_no_version.finding: Permutation-invariant (semantic) RSMs improve within-model retrieval on EgoObjects and mostly on Cityscapes. They also give somewhat more negative correlations with a classifier's own output JSD for most models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spatial alignment in RSM construction distorts within-model sample similarity in vision networks.

fits_no_version.finding: The same representations give CKA below 1 when RSMs are built semantically versus spatio-semantically (mean about 71-74%). Intra-model CKA differences vary by dataset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The RSM construction choice itself changes CKA-measured similarity structure.

record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the tabulated results. It describes the classifier-output correlations as generally low and acknowledges that it has not compared semantic RSMs with established retrieval techniques. CKA comparisons are described as qualitative, with no quantitative benchmark for choosing an RSM. Retrieval evidence is limited to the stated datasets and sampling procedures.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining EgoObjects database-size results (2.500 and 10.000) in Table 2 were omitted to stay within the 60-row limit; the 5.000 database condition is retained. The Spearman correlations in Table 4, individual CKA matrix cells and plotted distributions in Figures 15–17, and detailed layer-by-layer translation sensitivity plots in Figures 2 and 7 are also omitted. Table 2's other database sizes show the authors' stated trend that retrieval improvements decrease as database size grows.

untested.parts: All: no scaling or capability trend in cross-model alignment.
Shared features across seeds not assessed; seeds are used only for averaging.
All: no mapping or stitching between models.
Neighbour-count settings, out-of-distribution inputs, and cross-model dependence on kernel or dataset (only intra-model CKA varies by dataset).

record.verdict_notes: The study is mainly a methods paper on RSM construction; its bearing on representation convergence is limited to an appendix figure. The record's corr-* rows invert None/PI: Table 1 lists None first, then PI. For example, ResNet18 cosine is None -0.276 and PI -0.259 in the text layout, which conflicts with the row's -0.276 to -0.248. Verify against the PDF. The Table 3 RBF columns are garbled in the extracted text.

versions.untested_parts: Model scaling, capability, and alignment among independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
Alignment between vision and language representations of paired images and captions as model performance changes.
The study uses multiple seeds in some CKA analyses but does not test whether same-architecture models share features or subspaces across seeds.
Mapping, stitching, or otherwise transferring representations between models.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
The study tests dependence on RSM construction, kernels, and datasets, but not neighbour-count settings or out-of-distribution generalization as such.
Whether alignment plateaus or remains incomplete because of shared training data or objectives rather than a common model of reality.

rows.subject: ResNet18 and ResNet34 models
rows.stage_stated: trained on Tiny-ImageNet; seed count not stated in this comparison
rows.operation_detail: Compared CKA results when RSMs for the same representations were constructed as semantic or spatio-semantic.
rows.measure: CKA between RSMs
rows.value: Semantic and spatio-semantic RSM CKA differs; mean CKA is 71.0% for ResNet18 and 73.6% for ResNet34 in the figure description.
rows.note: The authors report the same representations do not have CKA 1 when their RSM construction differs; earlier layers differ more.
rows.check: Compares two RSM constructions of the same representations. It shows the measure differs, but measures no similarity between models.

rows.subject: ResNet18, ResNet34, and ResNet101
rows.stage_stated: three differently seeded models per architecture, trained from scratch
rows.operation_detail: Compared intra-model layer CKA matrices obtained from semantic and spatio-semantic RSMs.
rows.measure: Difference in CKA matrices
rows.value: The change is dataset-dependent; the authors report maximum changes between -0.2 and +0.2 for Tiny-ImageNet.
rows.note: This is a comparison of RSM choices, not a direct test of seed-to-seed feature convergence.
rows.check: Intra-model layer-to-layer CKA, not similarity between independently trained models.

rows.subject: ResNet18 and ResNet101 models
rows.operation_detail: Compared cross-model CKA matrices using semantic and spatio-semantic RSMs.
rows.measure: Difference in cross-model CKA
rows.value: Changes range from -0.175 to +0.025; the text says cross-model CKA is mostly negative for the majority of layers.
rows.note: The authors describe the change as modest and do not provide a quantitative benchmark for which RSM is preferable.
rows.check: Cross-model CKA is lower under semantic RSMs than under spatio-semantic ones for most layers (changes -0.175 to +0.025). Measured similarity depends on RSM construction, but the authors call the change modest. It is unclear whether the compared models differ by seed or by architecture.

relationships.condition: Cross-model linear CKA, ResNet18/ResNet101 on CIFAR100, semantic vs spatio-semantic RSMs
relationships.reason: Cross-model CKA drops under permutation-invariant RSMs for most layers (cka-cross), so measured similarity depends on RSM construction. The change is modest and reported only qualitatively from a figure.
relationships.display_finding: Cross-model CKA decreased modestly at most layers when representational similarity matrices were constructed to be permutation-invariant.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: EgoObjects retrieval, database size 5.000, all reported models and kernels
reader_labels.reason: Retrieval values differ between standard and permutation-invariant RSMs across models and kernels; the change is especially large for CLIPSeg and SAM (ego-clipseg-cos through ego-sam-rbf).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Cityscapes retrieval and ImageNet classifier-output correlations
reader_labels.reason: The PI effect is not uniform: Cityscapes inner-product results are mixed, and PI correlations with output JSD are weak and sometimes less negative or positive, depending on model and kernel (city-dino-ip through city-sam-rbf; corr-r18-cos through corr-dino-rbf).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CKA comparisons with different RSM construction and datasets
reader_labels.reason: The reported CKA comparisons change with semantic versus spatio-semantic RSM construction, and the intra-model pattern varies by dataset (cka-tiny, cka-datasets-intra, cka-cross).
